statements.lead: A focused wallet can be too limited.
statements.support: It may work well at first, but cannot grow around the needs users develop over time.

statements.lead: A feature-heavy wallet carries too much.
statements.support: Every permanent capability adds navigation, friction, dependencies, and security surface for every user.
Keep the wallet core clear and reliable, then add optional capabilities only when they solve a real user problem.

integrations.heading: Open entry. Curated production.
integrations.intro: Projects can apply through an open process. Production access is earned through qualification because integrations affect signing flows, permissions, navigation, performance, security, and the wider wallet experience.

steps.title: Apply
steps.description: Share the use case, target users, technical scope, permissions, maintenance plan, and distribution hypothesis.

steps.title: Qualify
steps.description: Salmon evaluates strategic fit, user value, technical feasibility, adoption potential, and product coherence.

steps.title: Build
steps.description: Salmon and the partner define ownership, milestones, dependencies, responsibilities, and implementation path.

steps.title: Validate
steps.description: Security, UX, signing flows, permissions, compatibility, maintainability, and operational impact are reviewed.

steps.title: Launch
steps.description: Approved integrations move into a controlled or production release with clear responsibilities and support expectations.

steps.title: Measure
steps.description: Activation, completed actions, repeat usage, retained cohorts, partner feedback, and maintenance status are tracked.

levels.title: Experimental
levels.description: Limited or controlled release to validate feasibility, UX, and demand.

levels.title: Verified
levels.description: Production-ready integration reviewed for security, UX, compatibility, and maintenance.

levels.title: Featured

integrations.disclaimer: Approval and promotion are separate decisions. Technical inclusion does not automatically guarantee endorsement or prominent placement.

distribution.heading: Integrations are not the goal. Usage is.
distribution.description: Salmon measures onboarding, completed actions, return usage, retained cohorts, integration performance, and partner feedback. What proves repeatable activation expands; what does not is improved, deprioritized, or stopped.

items.question: What is Salmon?
items.answer: An open-source, self-custodial, lightweight wallet built as open wallet infrastructure for Solana.

items.question: Can I use Salmon today?
items.answer: Yes. The Browser Extension, Web Wallet, and Android app are live. iOS is coming soon.

items.question: What is the Salmon Core?
items.answer: The focused wallet foundation for controlling assets, understanding signing requests, and interacting safely and reliably with Solana.

items.question: What is a Powerup?
items.answer: A selected modular integration that expands what users can do without permanently increasing the complexity of the wallet core.

items.question: Why use Salmon?
items.answer: Because access, signing clarity, and reliable interaction matter—not just storage.

items.question: Can I stake with Salmon?
items.answer: Not yet. Native in-wallet staking is coming soon. In the meantime, Salmon operates its own Solana validator with public, verifiable performance data.

items.question: What problem is Salmon solving?
items.answer: Strong projects can still struggle to reach active users. Salmon creates a more open, structured, and measurable path from selected integration to activation, feedback, repeat usage, and distribution proof.

items.question: Is Salmon permissionless production?
items.answer: No. Projects can apply through an open process, but production integrations require qualification, security review, product judgment, and operational accountability.

items.question: How are integrations selected?
items.answer: Salmon evaluates security, user value, UX coherence, technical compatibility, maintainability, partner commitment, and adoption potential.

items.question: What do Experimental, Verified, and Featured mean?
items.answer: They represent different levels of maturity, review, production readiness, and distribution support. Technical inclusion does not automatically guarantee endorsement or prominent placement.

items.question: How is Salmon different from other wallets?
items.answer: Salmon keeps the core wallet focused and uses selected modular integrations as an adoption strategy. Partners gain a credible path to users, while Salmon gains adoption through real use cases and existing communities.

items.question: Who is Salmon for?
items.answer: Solana-native applications, NFT communities, self-custody and security tools, infrastructure products, aligned builders, and users who value open infrastructure.

items.question: Why integrate Salmon?
items.answer: To reach users, gather product feedback, validate recurring behavior, and build measurable traction through a structured wallet integration path.

items.question: What does success look like?
items.answer: User activation, completed actions, repeat usage, retained cohorts, partner feedback, and evidence that an integration creates durable value.

items.question: Is Salmon open-source?
items.answer: Yes. The core software is public on GitHub.

items.question: How does Salmon approach signing safety?
items.answer: The core experience prioritizes helping users understand and approve signing requests. Every selected Powerup is evaluated for permissions, UX clarity, compatibility, dependencies, and user risk.

items.question: Is Salmon audited?
items.answer: Security is treated as an ongoing process: review, testing, audit readiness, and visible improvement.

items.question: What does "built in public" mean?
items.answer: Open-source code, visible progress, integration metrics, and accountable iteration. Salmon is meant to evolve in the open, not behind a closed roadmap.

items.question: What does community ownership mean in Salmon?
items.answer: Salmon is community-driven today and built toward ownership and governance structures that can align core assets and strategic oversight with the ecosystem it serves. Technical, security, and product reviews remain delegated operational responsibilities.
